course_name_original: Sistemas Avanzados de Tiempo Real y Empotrados
prerequisites: Intermediate knowledge of C and C++ programming language.
Ability to search and manage information via the Internet.
Average oral and written expression skills for debates and technical writing.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.
Students should know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students should possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Develop the potential of information and communication technologies in industrial production.
Apply the knowledge obtained in the master's degree to achieve greater efficiency, effectiveness, reliability, or security in an industrial environment.
Know the subjects and technologies that enable them to learn new methods and technologies, as well as provide them with sufficient versatility to adapt to new situations.
Use the acquired knowledge to maintain a critical and active attitude in the management of automation projects.
Analyze, design, and build industrial computer applications.

Effectively use a systematic approach to the development of industrial process control logic, using standardized techniques for the analysis, design, implementation, and documentation of the adopted solution.
Know the basic principles of robustness and usability of industrial software.
Apply an appropriate methodology for the analysis and design of real-time systems.

syllabus_topics: Development of software projects for real-time and embedded environments
Methods and techniques for embedded project development.
Methodology of the real-time system development process based on the UML language.
Requirements analysis, use cases, class diagrams.
Use of libraries for state machine implementation.
Specific considerations for the development of real-time and embedded systems
assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a grade of at least 5 out of 10 in the theoretical exam (E1) and at least 4 out of 10 in the course work (T1). If all established minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: Note = 0.2 * E1 + 0.8 * T1. Otherwise, the call's grade will be the minimum between the grade obtained with the formula and 4.0. The evaluation in extraordinary calls uses the same elements and criteria.
